utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Lisa Biersay on behalf of the Prosecution, and with me, we have Case Manager Thomas Laugel as well as my colleague Matthew Gillett.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, we understand that there is an issue we have to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sorry. Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Hadzic would address to the Chamber in private session, please, for some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There are no protective measures for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Just to give the Court an idea of the schedule today, I will be conducting the direct for the first witness. My colleague Ms. Clanton will be conducting the direct for the second witness, and the third witness will be handled by my colleague Ms. Dennehy. Then I will return for the last witness of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I may seek the Court's guidance on one matter. It pertains to which statements are part of the witness's 92 ter package. In our motion we had asked that his 1995 statement, as well as the one-page de minimis supplement be part of his package, and if that were granted, we would only use 30 minutes. And if we were only allowed to proceed with the 1995 statement, we would ask for 45 minutes in order to get those corrections on the record. And I read the decision as permitting us to tender both the statement and the supplement, but in an abundance of caution, I wanted to make sure that I understood that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the Court's reference, that would be tab 1 and tab 3. There is a tab 2 as well. That's the numbered -- the one with numbered paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You read the decision correctly, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I take it you can hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us your name and your date of birth and your ethnicity, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zeljko Cirba. I was born on the 3rd of January, 1964. I'm a Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are about to read the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. With this solemn declaration, you expose yourself to the penalty of perjury should you give misleading or untruthful information to the Tribunal. Would you now please read the solemn declaration the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very well. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cirba.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You can hear me well?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And are you comfortable where you're seated?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to 1995. Do you remember meeting with representatives from the Tribunal's Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And as a result of that meeting, do you remember signing a written statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 1. May I please ask the Registrar to display the English original of 65 ter 2228, which is dated 16 December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, if I could direct your attention to the screen before you. Do you recognise that document, the one on your right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: This is the statement that I provided to the investigators of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to the bottom of that page. Do you see a signature that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And whose signature do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: My own.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you sign each page of this statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in preparation for your appearance today, have you had an opportunity to review a translation of this statement in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you reviewed your statement in your language, did you find anything that you wanted to correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: There were a few corrections that I wanted to make, and we did make them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 2. May I please ask the registry for 65 ter 2228.1, which is the same as 65 ter 2228 but with handwritten paragraph numbers. And may I ask for some assistance, if it's agreeable to counsel, to provide Mr. Cirba with a hard copy of the numbered statement. Thank you. And for the benefit of the Court, we will first go to page 5 in the English, which is page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, directing your attention to paragraph 14. Do you have paragraph 14 before you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And towards the end of that paragraph, there is a sentence in parentheses: "(The Serbs always fired at the cars passing there.)" Did you want to change the word "always"?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to replace it with the word "often."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now directing your attention to paragraph 31, which is page 9 in the English version and page 7 in your version, Mr. Cirba. In that paragraph you mention that Mato Sabljak was abducted from Lovas and that he was still missing. Do you have more current information on Mr. Sabljak?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: That's correct. He was found in a mass grave, and then he was buried in Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when was his body found? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when that was. In any case, it was after the 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to May of this year, did you meet with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor to review the very statement that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 3. May I please ask the registry for 65 ter 2790, the English original dated 10 May 2012, the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document that's being displayed on the right side?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: This is a supplement to my statement, the one that I provided to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And again directing your attention to the bottom of the page, do you recognise any of the signatures there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, my own.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you reviewed this supplement in your language?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And was the supplement accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And with the corrections that you made to the 1995 statement, is that accurate as well?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If you were asked questions about the material contained in the 2012 clarification and in your 1995 statement, would you provide in substance the same information?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are these two statements truthful?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2228, which is the 1995 statement, as well as 2228.1, which is the version with paragraph numbers added, and finally 2790, which is the 2012 supplement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the original statement 2228 shall be assigned Exhibit Number P287. The statement with numbered paragraphs 2228.1 shall be assigned Exhibit Number P288. And the supplement statement under 65 ter 2790 shall be assigned Exhibit Number P289. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, I'd now like to ask you some questions about your written evidence. First I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 32, and in paragraph 32, you describe a mass grave at the Catholic cemetery in Lovas. When did you first receive information about that mass grave?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when was the exhumation of that mass grave actually conducted?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: In 1997, in the month of June or perhaps July.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why did it take so long to have the exhumation carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: That part of the state was under occupation. Therefore, no exhumations were possible at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "occupation," by whom?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: By the Yugoslav People's Army. At that time, the Serbs had proclaimed the so-called Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, did you attend this exhumation, any portions of it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why was that? Why did you attend?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I was the head of the municipality, and as the head of that municipality, I did not attend only that exhumation. I was also in Lovas, Tovarnik, Vukovar, Jelas, and in many other places where exhumations took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you spell the name of the village that you gave after Vukovar. Is it Jelas? Did I say that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Jelas is actually a forest near Lovas. One mass grave was discovered there at the beginning of 1998, one was discovered at the end of 1998, and a few individual graves. In Tovarnik there was a mass grave. In Vukovar there was a big mass grave containing over 900 bodies, and there were quite a few individual graves in Lovas, in the place itself, at the cemetery, in the houses, and we also found bodies scattered around the village of Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know whether these bodies were identified?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you know the ethnicity of the people who were recovered, the bodies that were recovered?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: In Lovas there were mostly Croats and other non-Serbs, namely, Hungarians and others.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 15, may I ask the registry for 65 ter 2222.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Cirba?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: This is a list of the villagers of Lovas who were buried in a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that the same mass grave that you discuss in paragraph 32 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How many bodies were recovered from this mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Sixty-eight.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, I direct your attention to page 2 of this exhibit, and I note that there are 66 names. Which names are missing from this list?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: A person named Kucinic from Tovarnik, and Ante Luketic from Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2222 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P290. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, turning to tab 8, may I ask the registry for 65 ter 2223. And this is a 92 ter package associated exhibit. And if we could focus on the first name, Jonak Rudolf.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, this document lists Rudolf Jonak as being buried in a mass grave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was he found in a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. He was found at the entrance to the graveyard, to the left. Immediately to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we won't tender that at this moment as it will be an associated exhibit and admitted that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cirba, I'd like to direct your attention to your discussions in your statement about people who were fleeing from other villages and coming to Lovas. From which villages were people fleeing?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: People were fleeing from Sotina, Berko [as interpreted], Tovarnik, Ilaca, Tompojevac [as interpreted] and many other places.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you spell the name of the place that you said after Sotina. Is it Berak or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Berak, B-e-r-a-k.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what was the majority ethnicity of those villages you've just listed?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The majority were Croatian, but there was a part where it was mixed. There were more Croats, but there were some Serbs. In Sotin there were more Croats than Serbs, but there were other ethnic groups and so on and so forth. In all the places I have mentioned, the majority were Croats, non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When the Croats fled to Lovas from Sotina, did they explain what was happening in Sotina that made them leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: They were afraid, because the Yugo army had infiltrated the area. There was shelling. There were casualties. Some people came to harm. People fled to Lovas because they were afraid, and they wanted to go beyond that area and reach Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "the Yugo army," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Speaking of Sotin, were you in Sotin for any event in July or August of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: There was a funeral of a citizen whose name I think was Drazen Luketic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened when you went to this funeral?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: There were planes flying over Sotin. They opened fire, machine-gun fire on the site where the funeral was being held probably in order to scare people. A rocket was launched on a bus or something like that. This was on the road leading to Tovarnik or, rather, to the crossroads, to Ilok. There was a lorry at the crossroads and a bus, and a rocket was launched at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you able to observe the village of Sotin in September or October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What did you see, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Houses that had been fired at, houses hit by shells to a certain extent, and there was almost no one in the street. So the people who had remained there were afraid, and unfortunately, many casualties were subsequently sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When the Croats fled to Lovas from Ilaca, did they explain what was happening in Ilaca that made them leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: It was because of the same things that happened in Sotina. The damage that was inflicted, the destruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When Croats fled to Lovas from Berak, did they explain what was happening in Berak to make them leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The reason was the same: Destruction, detaining people, killing people, fear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when the Croats fled to Lovas from Tovarnik, did they explain what was happening in Tovarnik that made them leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The reason is the same as in the case of these other places I have mentioned. There were a lot of casualties, aggression. Many people were killed. The tragedy was immense. There was a lot of fear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May I ask the registry how much time I have remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Shall we ask the Registrar how much you used?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I think I could do the math that way as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has used 24 minutes so far. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: On -- at some point in October, you -- as you describe in your statement, you left and went to Ilok; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And on the 17th of October, 1991, you left Ilok as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you were in Ilok for the time that you were there, were there other Croats who had fled from other areas and were now in Ilok?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you describe for the Trial Chamber from which villages you learned that these Croats were coming from?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Croats had come and non-Serbs as well from Sotina, Lovas, Tovarnik, Ilaca, Tompojevac, Bapska, Sarengrad, Mohova, and many other places.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you know why they came to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: They went to Ilok because they were afraid to remain in their places, because of fear. The same things happened in Berak, Sotina, Tovarnik, Ilaca, and unfortunately, in Lovas later on. People were afraid. The places would be infiltrated. I'm referring to the Yugo army again and their cronies. They would destroy the place. Many people came to harm and finally they were driven out, so they went there because they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why Ilok and not somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: They couldn't go any further. Everything was blocked off, cut off. Ilok was the last place people would reach. It was a mousetrap, as I have said. It wasn't possible to go any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Can you approximate the number of people who left Ilok when you did on the 17th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to give an estimate. It would be between 10- and 15.000, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you describe the scene of that mass departure to the members of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: People were told that a convoy was setting out in the morning, and people then arrived in the area of the vicinity of the bridge. They were searched there. There were some sort of lists, and some people were separated. People then entered cars, buses, lorries, tractors with trailers, whatever they had available, and they went to Croatia via Lipovac. It was terrible and very sad.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time I have no further questions, and I have no further time, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, how about the 92 ter package? Are you tendering it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the Registrar will mark them and circulate a memo about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Cirba. My name is Zoran Zivanovic, and I am defending Goran Hadzic in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, in your statement, I noticed that you weren't present in Lovas when this incident with the minefield occurred.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I also saw that you weren't in Lovas when the Yugoslav People's Army and, as you said, their cronies or helpers, when they launched an attack on Lovas on the 1st of October, they shelled it and they entered Lovas.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The attack on Lovas was on the 1st of October. I was there on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't mean the 1st of October. I meant the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of October you weren't in Lovas, when there was the shelling and when the JNA entered Lovas.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct. I wasn't in Lovas on the 10th of October, but in the previous period when there was the shelling of the church and so on and so forth, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us in your statement that in 1990, at the first freely held elections in Lovas, the Croatian Democratic Alliance won the election, the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that after the elections, you became the president of the Lovas local commune.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Of the Assembly of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Assembly of the local commune. At the time you were a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the situation in Lovas, the political atmosphere, in fact, was calm, but the Serbs and the former Communist delegates were boycotting the newly elected authorities.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, I have some information here that relates to that period in Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2803 is the number of the exhibit on our list. It's exhibit number 1. I don't think it is necessary to broadcast it to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting. I just wanted to make sure I understood the procedure. As the Trial Chamber will note, this is a -- is it counsel's intention to broadcast the document to the witness? And if so, we would oppose that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it -- in my opinion, it should not be shown to the public and to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Zivanovic, we'll do that. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I also understand that the person from whom the statement originates will not be identified to the witness. I understood that was our protocol for using these types of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have information according to which sometime in the second half of April or perhaps at the end of April 1990, a meeting was held in the village of Bogdanovci, a meeting of local HDZ representatives. It was convened by Tomislav Mercep. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: It wasn't a meeting. It was just a matter of people socialising, but I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We also have information according to which during that period Tomislav Mercep was the coordinator of all HDZ activities in the municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't involved in those structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the other information we have, the meeting was held in the local commune in the village of Bogdanovci, and about 30 presidents and vice-presidents of local HDZ branches attended it.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. I wasn't present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who attended the meeting from Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know Jovo Milas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what he was at the time? What sort of position did he have in the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: He was president of HDZ, and he was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Josip Gracanac?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was he at the time in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know. I think he was -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Marin Vidic, aka Bili?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a position of any kind in the HDZ in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I think he was a member of the HDZ committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the persons who attended the meeting inform you of the subjects discussed at the meeting, what happened at the meeting? Did they tell you anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, were you in contact with those people or were you on bad terms with them?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. We were on good terms, but we didn't discuss that subject matter. As the president of the local commune I was involved in certain other affairs, and it concerned utilities, organisation, and so on and so forth. That was the work involved in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you were involved in other affairs, what sort of affairs were these people involved in? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: You'd have to put that question to them. They were performing their professional duties. Mr. Milas was a lawyer. Mr. Josip was unemployed at the time. Marin Vidic worked in the community as an agronomist. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you knew what sort of things they did as HDZ members. I'm not asking you about their normal duties.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I said they were HDZ members. There was an HDZ committee, but I wasn't present at the meeting, so I don't know. I wasn't a member of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If they didn't inform you, did anyone else inform you of the fact that on that occasion Tomislav Mercep - I'm speaking about the meeting in Bogdanovci - Tomislav Mercep said that according to the instructions he had received from the central HDZ organs in Osijek, the HDZ would be subject to military organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time a decision was taken according to which some sort of technical service was to be established as part of this idea?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And as for a military service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As for a medical service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information in my possession, after the meeting in Bogdanovci, a meeting was held in the village of Lovas, and it was attended by certain individuals. I'll ask you whether you know them. Mijo Kolic or, rather, Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know Kolic not Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Franjo Krizmanic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Branko Krizmanic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Josip Badnjak?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Badnjak, no. Badanjak perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Badanjak, I apologise. Josip Filic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Madzarevic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Keser also known as Braca?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I think I know whom you are talking about, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tomislav Rendulic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And Franjo Mujic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that these people and the three persons I mentioned earlier on then went about establishing a military, technical and medical service in the village of Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the village of Lovas had about 1.400 inhabitants, I believe. 1.441 -- 1.661, I apologise, at the time, and 1.441 of them were Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately how many HDZ members there were in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that information.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "You told us that there were 1.681 inhabitants," not 1.661.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the following. You were the president of the local commune in Lovas at the time. Many people from the HDZ were involved in these activities I have been describing and you knew nothing about it. How is that possible in such a small place? How can such a thing happen?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I was involved in the duties I have told you about. Up until Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May -- well, after that event the Crisis Staff -- a Crisis Staff was established. I was a member of the Crisis Staff then, and then I had more information on the situation in the village and contact with the Serbs that I have mentioned. We had a lot of such contact up until that point in time, and as the president of the local commune, I together with all the other inhabitants of the village strove to ensure that nothing happened in Lovas. So after the HDZ victory in Lovas, all the Serbs who had certain official positions retained them. Moreover, some of these positions were subsequently confirmed. I have mentioned that. Nothing ugly happened, and any incident that could have occurred, well, we tried to deal with such incidents. That concerned going to negotiations, daily contact that was established, and this was very important, I think. All we wanted was peace. We didn't want harm to come to anyone. We wanted to protect each other. And I was also referring to the meeting with Mr. Lovric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to these activities that I mentioned, they took place in April. The event in Borovo village was on the 2nd of May, and these preparations, I assume, occurred before the events in Borovo village. But what I want to ask you is the following: When you say that a Crisis Staff was established after the events in Borovo village at the beginning of May, let's say --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: In the course of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of May, yes. Sir, did that Crisis Staff have a technical service, a medical service, a military service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff had to ensure that everyone in Lovas protected each other. That was its main role, and the members of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Krizmanic, Mr. Rendulic, myself, and many others frequently attended meetings, went to negotiations, spoke with people, tried to calm things down. We quite simply wanted to ensure that peace prevailed in the village of Lovas. We didn't want any harm to come to anyone. We all strove to achieve this objective, and no Serbs came to harm of any kind. Especially when people were coming from villages that had been torched, when there were people who were being killed, people passing through cornfields with their young children to reach our place, all we did was to try to ensure that no harm came to anyone. That was our priority, but naturally there were also guards that had been set up around the place. We had summoned all the inhabitants of Lovas to join in and to ensure that we were able to protect each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were some lists of people compiled at the time, and those were the people that would be involved in the protection of the village?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. There were guards around the village, at the entrance to the village. Sometimes they were mounted, sometimes not, but those guards existed in the entire municipality of Vukovar. The -- we were afraid that somebody might storm into the village and cause problems. Those guards were very benevolent. They let people through and really no harm ever came to anybody, as far as I know at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, are you still trying to get an answer to your question whether that Crisis Staff had a medical service, a technical service and a military service?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're still on that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask you this: Within the Crisis Staff was there a technical service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Within the framework of the Crisis Staff there was no technical service. If you're asking about a medical service, yes, we did have a doctor, Dr. Kacar, who was a Serb. He was a very fair person, very, very fair. And together with a few women who were nurses and who wanted to assist him, they worked in the old school as of the end of September, and they helped people who had arrived from Tovarnik and who were wounded there. So they were administered first aid and all the other necessary medical service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was in the month of September, but we are still talking about the months of April and May. According to the information that I have, in the village of Lovas, the head of the medical service was Franjo Mujic and then Branko Krizmanic.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I've never heard that before. Dr. Kacar was the head of our medical service. He was the only doctor that we had, so he was the only one capable of occupying that position. The other two are not doctors, those people who you have just mentioned. One is an electrician, and the other is a worker in a company, a maintenance worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that we have, the task of the medical service was to get supplies for being able to assist the wounded in the future. They were tasked with obtaining medicines and medical supplies that would be necessary in case of a future conflict. However, my question is this: Those two, were they members of the Crisis Staff, Franjo Mujic and Branko Krizmanic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. I believe that there were 12 members of the Crisis Staff. I can remember some of them off the top of my head, and as of -- for the others, my memory would have to be jogged.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about Markica Gracanac or Marko Gracanac, was he a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I can tell you the names of those that I remember. Jozo Milas, Mr. Madzarevic, Mr. Rendulic, Mr. Krizmanic, myself, Djuka Filic, and several others. Twelve altogether, but my memory would have to be jogged. It is possible that the gentleman that you've just mentioned was also a member, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you said Madzarevic, did you mean Ivo Madzarevic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What were his tasks in the staff? According to the information that I have, he was the head of the military service in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. It wasn't a military service. There was no military service. However, he was one of the men who assigned people to the guard duty. All citizens - Croats, Serbs, and Hungarians - were invited to join the village guard. Some of the Serbs did indeed join, because we had explained to them that we wanted to keep watch and guard each other and protect each other. That's how things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that we have, the military service that was set up after the meeting in the village of Bogdanovci was supposed to train the armed members of the HDZ and to build a concept of warfare in the municipality of Vukovar in case the independent state of Croatia was not established peacefully. That's the information we have.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't share the same information. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Ivo Madzarevic was not the head of the military but of the technical service, and Marko Gracanac was the head of the military service according to the information that we have.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the HDZ in Lovas, can you remember how many Serbs were members of the same party?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Several, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How come that only a few Serbs joined the HDZ, why not more?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the HDZ and as the president of the local commune in the village of Lovas, were you not interested in finding out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: My job was different. My job was to treat everybody equally, and I did at the time. I do now. When I was the president of the local commune and the president of the municipality and now that I'm the deputy prefect of the county, Partisan membership is everybody's right, and everybody can join any party or not join any party at all. That's everybody's choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you advocated the equality of all the citizens irrespective of their ethnic affiliation, did it not strike you as odd that there is a disbalance between Croatian HDZ membership and the Serb membership of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: At the time there were other parties as well, so the citizens could opt for any of them. There was the HSLS, the Peasants' Party, and many other parties existed. So not everybody was a member of the HDZ. Just as today people have every right to be members of any party or not to have any party affiliation at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time you were on good terms with all the citizens of the Serb ethnicity who resided in Lovas, I assume.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You had frequent contacts, both official and non-official.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Of course. We played football together. We talked. We socialised. We worked together. Everything was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from them, that they had objections towards the HDZ and its policies?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, never. We talked about things that were more important at the time. When there was no imminent threat of war, we had other problems that we had to deal with concerning electricity, water, rubbish collection, roads and things like that. Later on we talked not once about ways to protect each other. For example, when women and children were sent to the coast, everybody went, Serbs and Croats. When we had talks with Mr. Lovric, we were all there and we said to both ethnicities that nothing should happen to them. When the members of the guard arrived in Lovas in July, they did not encounter a single problem. No houses were searched. Nothing happened. And everybody knows that well, and if they want to tell the story correctly and in a fair manner, that's what they're going to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm still talking about the months of April and May 1991. Do you know that the Crisis Staff or one of its services at that time obtained two kilos of explosives?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time the manufacture of explosives was organised in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that some explosive devices were used to intimidate the Serbian population in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was one incident. Somebody threw something into Mr. Devcic's courtyard. I believe that that was all. There was no damage. We don't know what happened. The police were called. They did their job, and I don't know what the result of the investigation was. That's all I know about incident. Although you did not ask me, I believe that there was a farm belonging to a man whose name I can't remember in the direction of Vukovar. There was a problem there, but I don't know what that problem was. Every time the police intervened, I don't know the outcome of any of the investigations. After those incidents again we sat down, we discussed the situation. We condemned those incidents and the perpetrators thereof and we insisted that the police should be called to do their job and to punish those who were responsible, because those situations were in favour of nobody. That's why we tried to prevent them and avoid them. And after that everything was back to normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in July or perhaps in August 1990, 1990, I'm talking about the year 1990, on the premises of the Vukovar HDZ, a meeting of the Municipal Board of the HDZ was held pursuant to the instruction -- instructions of the central HDZ board in Osijek, and that meeting was called by Tomislav Mercep? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I don't. At that time, I was merely a member of the party, nothing else. I was not a member of any party structure at a higher level. I was just a member of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that already at that time a decision was taken about the establishment of volunteer detachments?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know either, I suppose, that the main criterion for recruiting people into those volunteer detachments was that they were supporters of the HDZ in its endeavour to create an independent state of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the political option of the HDZ, to create an independent state of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: The political option of all the citizens of Croatia was to create a state. At the beginning there would have been a confederation of Yugoslavia. I don't know the details. Those were political negotiations at the very top of the state. We did not have a say in any of that, nor did anybody actually consult us about any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the political option of all the citizens of Croatia was to create an independent state of Croatia, do you also imply Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Sir, there was a referendum, and the referendum showed how many citizens wanted an independent state. I believe that the result was about 90-plus per cent. That means that the citizens of Croatia were invited to participate in the referendum and decide on that, and based on that, I conclude that that was the will of the majority. You can check the result, obviously. Some didn't participate, some voted differently, but a majority was in favour of creating an independent state of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking about what you know. According to what you knew at the time, how did Serb -- Serbs vote in the referendum? Did they also opt for the independent state of Croatia? I believe that there were over 10 per cent of Serbs residing in Croatia at the time.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I really don't know how people voted. It was a secret ballot. You could just say yes or no, and you did it secretly, unbeknownst to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So when you answered that all Croatians of citizens -- all Croatian citizens were in favour of an independent state of Croatia, you can't say exactly how many were against, how many did not participate and what the position of the Serbs was? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I told you that everybody could vote in the referendum. Every citizen of Croatia was invited to vote the way they wanted. There is information as to how many voted, how many voted against, how many voted in favour, and how many did not participate in the referendum. I can tell you exactly how I voted. I don't know how the others did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear at the time that the Serbs actually boycotted that referendum, that the Serbian political parties invited the Serbs to boycott the referendum and that the Serbs really did not vote in that referendum?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1990, in the months of either July or August when a decision was taken -- or, rather, did you observe that in your midst that there was an increased demand for permits to carry weapons? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a certain number of citizens from Lovas reported to join those volunteer detachments?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "volunteer detachments."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: A while ago I said that at a meeting in Vukovar there was a decision according to which volunteer detachments were to be established. That was August 1990. And HDZ supporters were to be members, and they were to be armed. I'd like to know whether you heard that in July or August and subsequently that such a volunteer detachment was established.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have information according to which Marko Gracanac formed such a detachment in Lovac with 120 members. Since you lived in Lovas, is it possible that you were not aware of fact?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: You mean there were 120 men bearing arms or they were members of the detachment? I don't understand what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. I said that Marko Gracanac established such a detachment with 120 members.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard that in 1990, it was suggested that force should be used to dispel a meeting that was to be held by the Serbian Democratic Party on the 1st of May at the Adica site, the Adica tourist site?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in April and May 1990, at meetings of the HDZ Municipal Committee initiative was launched to establish a certain amount of control over the Serbian population in the territory of Vukovar municipality, and Lovas is part of that municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I said that I was not a member of any committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you were an HDZ member. I assume that you also had certain duties as a party member, especially since you were later elected to become president of the local commune, I assume that it was on the basis of the results that you attained in the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't a member of the committee, of any committees, and I have described my duties, the duties that I performed during the period that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the village of Bogdanovci, a review of the volunteer troops was held?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I saw that on television, but as to what exactly happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was in September 1990. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that there was a review of a volunteer detachment in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information we have, it's not only that there was such a review but the entire HDZ Executive Committee was present.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any reviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that buses and cars were used to transport a detachment from Lovas with volunteers to go to the review in Bogdanovci?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know how many people went. There were probably some people who went. As to whether it was a review or meeting, what exactly happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information we have, between 1.500 and 2.000 volunteers participated in that review from various places, not just from Lovas.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another question: At the time you worked in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: In the agricultural cooperative Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time the Lovas agricultural cooperative provided cash loans to members of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: That's the first time I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that same cooperative, Jozo Milas worked with you.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. He was a lawyer. I was a trainee agronomist. I worked for a year and my contract was then terminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information we have, the agricultural cooperative in Lovas then handed out cash loans to a certain number of HDZ members who were at the same time members of a volunteer detachment. Officially the loan was to be used to buy livestock or agricultural equipment, but in fact, it was agreed that the money should be used to buy weapons. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. The Lovas cooperative, like many other cooperatives, provided loans for the agricultural sector and so on and so forth, but I'm not aware of what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, Rendulic Adam was the director of the cooperative.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct and that is still the case today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to our information, as part of this agreement approval was given for 50 or 20 such loans, the amount of which was between 6- to 7.000 dinars. That was the price of a rifle at the time.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know whether Franjo Mujic received a loan of any kind from the agricultural cooperative?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I don't know. I had nothing to do with that. I was an agronomist and worked in the fields, unfortunately very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is indeed, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Witness, we take the first break now. We will come back at 11.00. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cirba, I'll now move on to the period between the 10th and 15th of September, 1991. Several weeks before the shelling of Lovas, we also have information according to which at that time on the premises of the municipality of Vukovar -- or, rather, in the Secretariat for National Defence weapons were distributed to HDZ members and members of the volunteer detachments. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to that information, the following went to those premises to take over weapons from Lovas: Antun Vidic, Nikica Maric, Mile Hodak, Stipo Filic, Josip Filic, and perhaps some others for whom we don't have precise information. I would first like to know whether you know these citizens of Lovas.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that they received these weapons, that they went to Vukovar, to the premises of Vukovar municipality, to the premises of the Secretariat of National Defence in order to receive these weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to our information, the first two Kalashnikovs that arrived in Lovas were distributed to Jovo Milas and Josip Gracanac. This was in January 1991. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No. You'd have to ask them about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And we have information according to which three or four Kalashnikovs were distributed to members of the HDZ Executive Committee in Lovas. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Here the names mentioned in addition to the two I've already mentioned, the names mentioned are Josip Badanjak, Branko Krizmanic, Franjo Mujic, Ivo Madzarevic, Markica Gracanac, Josip Filic, and Franjo Krizmanic.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you another document, D4 on the Defence list. It's in English but I'll read it out and you will hear the interpretation. I'll just read out the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I apologise. I just want to put my glasses on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the document. It's from our list, 1D141. It's the fourth document on our list. It's to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's in English and I'll read it out. The title is: [In English] "Army controls Bosut, Danube river territories." [Interpretation] And I'll only read the first paragraph which I'm interested in and then we will discuss it. [In English] "15 October, TANJUG. All places between the Bosut and Danube rivers are from today under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army units and the Serbian reservists, army sources have stated." [Interpretation] What I would like to know is since at the time, 15th of October, you were in the area, not in Lovas but you were in the area, what I'd like to know is whether this information is correct. Does it reflect the situation on the ground at the time, or at least the situation in the area that you were in at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: As far as I know, this information is from the 15th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Ilok left or fell on the 17th of October, so it wasn't occupied at the time. I don't know about the other places. The other places were up to Lovas. There was Opatovac, everything else was occupied. Muhovo remained, Sarengrad and Bapska up to Ilok remained. I'm not sure whether those places were also under occupation or, as it says here, under JNA control. Ilok wasn't because we left Ilok on the 17th. I know the other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is what it says in the same paragraph. "[In English] They went on to say that the Croatian forces have been completely destroyed in this area and are only holding Ilok now. However, according to an agreement between JNA representatives and the Croatian forces, the town should be handed over to the army on 17 October." [Interpretation] Is this the reflection of the situation as it was at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I know that there were negotiations about Ilok. However, I don't know how they went, but I know that we left Ilok on the 17th. On the 15th, Ilok was still in the hands of the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number D15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we have D3, tab 3, 1D140. Tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question, Mr. Cirba, do you know that a trial was on in Belgrade for crimes committed in Lovas against a large group of people? I believe that you testified in that case, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read some of names from here and ask you whether you remember them. Ljuban Devetak, Milan Devcic, Milan Radojcic, Zeljko Krnjaic. I won't go on. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, were they found guilty and sentenced in that case?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: We attended the reading of the first instance Trial Chamber decision. The 14 accused were all found guilty, but I can't remember how many years they were each sentenced to. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would tender this document into evidence. It is an orally announced judgement, not in the written form, but it is orally pronounced by the War Crime Chamber of the High Court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May I inquire the purpose for which it's being tendered? Is it being tendered to show the fact that there was a judgement or is it being tendered for the substantive information contained in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For both purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We would object to it being tendered for substantive evidence, but we would not object to it being tendered to show the fact that there was, in fact, a proceeding and the outcome of that proceeding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not understand the point of this objection. I don't know whether the Prosecution stated that these persons are not guilty for this crime described in this judgement, or I really cannot understand the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I may. My point is that to the extent that there are substantive issues and fact findings that this Trial Chamber has to make, that this document will not supersede those findings. So this document, when admitted, we believe should be admitted for the purpose of saying, yes, there was a proceeding, these people were charged, and they were found guilty, but not for -- and I haven't had a chance to read it in detail. Not for all the individual findings that are made with respect to each person. That's the nature of the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, could you explain to us the relevance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The relevance of this document is in that because these people were found guilty and convicted for -- both for the attack on Lovas on 10 of October, 1991, and for incident in minefield, which is a part of indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Not a problem, Your Honour. If that is the purpose for which it is being tendered we do not object to that. What we would object to is if Mr. Zivanovic pointed to pages 2 or 3 and said, "We believe that the Trial Chamber should accept each and every finding made by another court." So if it's just the fact of the conviction and the charges, then we do not have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have never said that this Trial Chamber must accept anything from this -- from this judgement. It is on you to assess -- to properly assess this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number D16. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cirba, I'd like to thank you. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Thank you also, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Redirect, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you, Mr. Cirba, on page 31, line 12, of the temporary transcript, you mentioned someone named Devcic. You said something was thrown -- it's not in your statement. It was when you were testifying and that page number is just so that everyone else knows where it is. You mentioned the name Devcic. You said something was thrown in his courtyard. Do you know the first name of this Devcic? And the reason --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: I believe that his first name is Bozo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So it's just to confirm. It's not the Mica Devcic that's in your statement at paragraph 17, or is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. It was not part of my cross-examination. I never asked anything about Devcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. You did not -- counsel did not ask, but in the witness's response he said the word -- it was thrown in the courtyard of Devcic, and I'm clarifying to whom is he referring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So what we have on the record is the last name Devcic, and I just want to know if you know the first name, and if it's related to the Devcic that's in your statement.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Bozo Devcic. He is Mica's father, Milan Devcic's father, a Croat by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I understand you correct, Mica -- when you say the word "Mica," is that a short name for Milan?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO CIRBA
utterances.text: Yes. I repeat. We're talking about a Croat, Bozo Devcic. Something was thrown into his courtyard. I don't know what. And his son is Milan Devcic. I suppose that his nickname is Mica, because we knew him as Mica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cirba, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You're now released as a witness. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom, and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, with the Court's permission, I wanted to seek guidance on some proposed 65 ter exhibits. Specifically, we -- in our fifth motion, we sought to add some material. We have spoken to the Defence, and regarding three of the items they do not have any objections. We anticipate that perhaps we will be using them for the upcoming witnesses, so I thought I would see with the Trial Chamber if the Trial Chamber is willing at this time to consider the admission -- sorry, adding to our 65 ter exhibit list proposed exhibit 6350, which is a video of some relevant areas in Lovas; 6351, which are pictures taken at the same time and also of Lovas; and 2508A, as in apple, which is a photo album.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the Defence does not object; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So those three documents can be added to your 65 ter list, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And finally, Your Honours, there are some logistics involved in switching positions with my colleagues, and I just apologise in advance for -- for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No problem. Can we bring in the next witness, Ms. Clanton?

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. First of all, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us your name, your date of birth, and your ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ivan Mujic, 1954, Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 1954? Do you have a precise date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 1st of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are -- you are about to read the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. I have to point out to you that by taking that declaration you expose yourself to the penalty of perjury should you give misleading or untruthful information to the Tribunal. Could you now read the solemn declaration, please, the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Clanton, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mujic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: If you have any difficulty hearing me, please let the Court know right away. Do you recall giving a statement to investigators of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: I would like to ask that 65 ter 2235, a statement dated the 6th of February, 1996, be placed on the monitor. This is tab number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Mr. Mujic, do you recognise this as the statement you gave?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll to the bottom of the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: And prior to testifying today, did you have an opportunity to review a translation of this statement in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today that you were asked when you gave the statement, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of this statement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2235 into evidence. We would also like to tender 65 ter 2235.1 into evidence, which is at tab 2. This is the same statement of the witness, but we've added paragraph numbers for ease of reference to both the English and B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just make a suggestion. There won't be any objection in respect of adding paragraph numbers to any statement that's tendered as long as that's the only change. So if it's agreeable to the Prosecution, just to reduce the number of documents we have in court, we could just go with the .1 document, but it's up to the Prosecution. I'm just offering that as a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that's a good idea. The reason we had wanted to tender both 2235 and 2235.1 is that the original is the one that the witness has signed. We've marked the PDF with his signature on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the .1 has no signature on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It does also. Okay. So we can just admit the numbered one; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The numbered statement under 65 ter 2235.1 shall be assigned Exhibit Number P296. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for ease of reference for the witness, I would like to suggest that we provide him with a paper copy of the numbered statement, if the usher could assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: I would like to ask that 65 ter 06276, which is an aerial image, be placed on the monitor in front of the witness, please. This is tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: Mr. Mujic, I'm first going to ask you a few questions about what you observed in Lovas right after the town was occupied. First, do you recognise the town depicted in this image?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
utterances.text: What is the name of this town?

utterances.speaker: IVAN MUJIC
utterances.text: Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MS. CLANTON
